{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZvJPrg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDVEg8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 137, "title": "Show real current JST dates instead of projecting PC-VAN activity into 1996", "body": "## Problem

The terminal intentionally projects modern activity timestamps onto a fictional late-November 1996 calendar. A user visiting OLT now sees year 1996 in attendance/speech records and finds this misleading and confusing. The user explicitly wants **current, real-world date/time** displayed for activity happening now, while preserving the **nostalgic 1996-style PC-VAN interface**. The historical service aesthetic does not require a fictional clock.

This mapping is not a display-only string: `src/calendar.ts` projects timestamps using a stored `historical-calendar` anchor; forum/mail/conference/OLT/NetNews headers and scheduled-mail entry/confirmation depend on it, and `src/ai/setting.ts` still explicitly places fictional residents in late 1996. An isolated OLT string change would leave inconsistent years and the scheduled-mail interface confusing.

## Expected outcome

- Use **actual operational timestamps** in the existing fixed **JST (UTC+09:00)** presentation timezone for new and existing local activity. If someone sends a message today in 2026, their OLT line, forum post, mail and relevant service headers should show **2026** and the genuine local date/time, not 1996 or an elapsed-day projection.
- Keep PC-VAN's classic menus, terminal-only interaction, Japanese text and period-inspired presentation; distinguish stylistic nostalgia from chronological deception.
- Preserve genuine **historical source dates and authored archival examples** labeled 1993/1995/1996/1997 rather than relabeling historical reference content as current news. For locally seeded fictional conversations, their stored UTC timestamps should be displayed accurately. Do not rewrite timestamps or messages in existing IndexedDB stores/backups.
- Reconcile the resident generation setting with a current-date world where needed: characters should not insist the calendar year is 1996 or reinterpret a present-day user's remarks as future events just because the UI imitates 1990s PC-VAN. Keep established fictional personas and sensible retro-community tone; source/research documentation can still describe the 1996–1997 service being reconstructed.
- **Scheduled local mail** `WRITE-AT` must show and accept the user's actual upcoming `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` JST date and convert it correctly to UTC, enforcing the existing real 30-day horizon. Preserve already-approved pending deliveries at their stored absolute instants and across backup/restore. Never re-interpret old user-specified real timestamps as 1996 or change when deliveries release.
- Existing `historical-calendar` records/backups may remain readable as historical metadata if needed for safe compatibility, but must **not drive routine date projection**. Avoid complicated migration/reseed UI; no mandatory factory reset merely to fix timestamps.

## Context

Latest checked `main`: `ecf7a006371b8e605d4f9b54b0566bf85e78df9c` (OLT #135 merged); recheck before coding.

Key current code:
- `src/calendar.ts`: `historicalAnchor()` anchors operational dates to November 18–24, 1996; `serviceDate()` projects user-generated timestamps; `scheduleTime()` and `scheduleInstant()` map scheduling input through the fictional year. `isHistorical()` and `initialCalendar()` handle legacy anchors.
- `src/ai/setting.ts`: `historicalSetting` actively instructs all generated forum posts, mail and OLT to inhabit late 1996. `docs/local-ai.md` calls this a period knowledge horizon distinct from operational time. Update the temporal framing consistently without erasing era research or source provenance.
- `src/olt.ts`, `src/forums.ts`, `src/mail.ts`, `src/conference.ts`, `src/netnews.ts`, `src/navigation.ts`, `src/sections.ts` and any other `serviceDate` callers present terminal timestamps. Check all dynamic services instead of fixing OLT alone.
- `src/storage/schema.ts` validates the `CALENDAR_SETTING` record and scheduled-mail relation; `src/storage/repository.ts` stores operational UTC timestamps and backup/restore state. Ensure changes in time *presentation* do not rewrite historical/user records or break import validators.
- `tests/calendar.spec.ts`, scheduled-mail, OLT, forum/mail/NetNews and reset/restore tests may assert fictional 1996 date strings. Update narrowly and preserve independent deterministic clock/date-boundary assertions.
- This is user-requested **date correctness**, not a request for actual backend connectivity, contemporary hosted PC-VAN, or removal of historically authentic screen/service references.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md). English Issue/PR/docs; Japanese in-world UI.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Terminal session entry and live OLT speech/arrival/leave times use the **real displayed year, date and JST clock** from the actual stored operational timestamp. Real-time/Olt simulated dates are not silently moved to November 1996; show a four-digit year where needed to remove ambiguity.
- [ ] Forum, locally generated/seeded replies, mail and scheduled delivery, conference, local NetNews and other time-stamped local services show consistent real JST dates. Actual archived 1996 sample material and period reference citations retain their original dates and explanatory labels.
- [ ] In fake-clock production-browser journeys at two modern dates (including 2026), a human can join OLT, speak, receive a mocked resident reply, read a forum/mail item and see the expected actual year/day/minute. Include midnight/year rollover and at least two browser timezone settings, ensuring JST presentation is independent of the device timezone.
- [ ] `WRITE-AT` accepts an upcoming actual **2026-or-later** JST date within 30 elapsed days; invalid/impossible/past/out-of-window inputs fail without changing drafts or delivery records. Confirm that release, cancellation, repeated ticks, cross-tab arbitration, JSON export/import and previously scheduled absolute instants remain correct.
- [ ] Existing worlds, saved `historical-calendar` metadata, and legacy/imported backups can be opened and rendered with real operational dates **without deleting, re-seeding or rewriting posts/messages**. Preserve backup atomicity and restore validation; no new migration/backfill UI.
- [ ] Update AI shared setting/prompt constraints so resident conversations are not incorrectly date-locked to 1996 while retaining the familiar retro communication culture, established characterization, limited model context and source-provenance disclosures. Verify prompts against modern user messages and that OLT/mail/forum continue to use only their permitted contextual data.
- [ ] Preserve the retro terminal-only UI, ordinary handles, consented local WebLLM, budgets, offline behavior, IME/focus, stable member identities and current OLT #135 reply/presence improvements.
- [ ] Update README, calendar/mail/local-AI/storage docs and historical-accuracy limitations to distinguish a **1996-inspired service reproduction** from the **present-day interaction date**. Run `npm test` and `npm run build`, report actual results including failures; avoid unnecessary new test cases.

## Optional validation

Manual walkthrough on the published build at the actual current JST date and a scheduled-mail example crossing midnight. A manual real-model test may reveal generation's year confusion but is not a mandatory GPU/download dependency.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Fake-clock browser tests, IndexedDB persistence and production build cover this change pre-merge; deployment follows the normal Pages workflow.
